## Dial 1.0.19 — 27 Oct 2026

- **Studio: Beauty works on your real face.** Studio now finds your face for real, with Apple's own Vision face finder (the same one Photos uses): the face, its outline, eyebrows, eyes, nose and lips as 76 points, and which way the head is turned or tilted — ten times a second, from a small copy of the camera picture, in a helper process of Dial's audio engine (`dial-engine --face`, the same signed program, so macOS asks nothing new). Every Beauty control sits on those points now: skin smoothing and even tone cover the face and neck and never blur the eyes, brows, lips or nostrils; eye brightening and bigger eyes centre on your eyes; lip tint and whiter teeth follow the lip lines; blush sits on the cheekbones; face slimming, the V-line jaw, nose, chin and forehead are gentle pinches anchored to the jaw, nose wings, chin and hairline, and they turn and tilt with your head (the side turned away is pinched less). Blur, Colour and Picture backgrounds keep your head, hair and shoulders by the real outline. The points are smoothed over time so nothing jitters, a face is held for a second if a frame misses it, and the picture glides between answers. The Look tab shows **Face: found** or **looking**; the centred guess is used only until a face is found (or where the face finder can't run). The sliders' middle values were tuned to look natural on a real face, and the presets reworked on the new masks: Punchy stays exactly as it was, with three new relatives — Punchy soft, Punchy warm and Punchy cool — and Soft film is kept (23 presets; hotkeys and OSC reach 35 slots). On a Mac without the face finder, the skin-tone finder and the centred guess work as before.

- **Dial's records live in the dashboard's own database.** Codes, computers, crashes and the dashboard stamp moved from the key-value store to a database of their own in the dashboard's Databases tab (no Cloudflare limits) — one `kv` table the Worker makes itself, with every record's expiry and listing details kept. The release script copies the old key-value store into it right before the new Worker goes live and catches up whatever the old Worker wrote meanwhile, so nothing is lost and a code works the same before and after; expired claims and old crash reports are swept out by the hourly tidy-up. The old `dial-kv` namespace is left in place for the owner to delete by hand once the new Worker has run a few days.

### Install

Dial is a Mac app (Apple silicon — M1 and later). One download: `Dial_<version>_aarch64.dmg`.

- **With Pour:** `curl -fsSL https://ipconfig.co.network/pour/install | sh` then `pour install --cask dial`
- **By hand:** open the DMG and drag Dial into Applications. First launch: `xattr -cr /Applications/Dial.app` (Dial is self-signed, not notarized).
- Per-app volume and the equaliser need macOS 14.4 or later.
- Earlier Windows, Linux, ChromeOS, FreeBSD and Intel Mac builds stay on the releases page but are no longer updated.
